subject: Archaeology
title: Richard III Under a Parking Lot
description: A fast breakdown of Richard III Under a Parking Lot for builders.

hook.text: In 2012, archaeologists dug up a parking lot in Leicester, England. They found a king.

buildup.text: Richard III died in the Battle of Bosworth in 1485. His body was lost for over 500 years.

discovery.text: The skeleton showed severe scoliosis and battle wounds, including a blade strike that split the skull.

twist.text: DNA from a living descendant confirmed the identity. The king had been buried under a friars' church.

climax.text: Richard III was reburied in Leicester Cathedral in 2015 with full royal honors, 530 years after his death.

punchline.text: A king lost for five centuries was found under a parking space.

quiz.question: How was the skeleton confirmed as Richard III?
options: DNA from a living descendant confirmed the identity
A royal seal was found buried alongside the body

details.summary: In 2012, archaeologists found the skeleton of King Richard III beneath a Leicester parking lot, confirming a local legend about the lost burial of the king killed at the Battle of Bosworth in 1485. DNA analysis, battle injuries, and scoliosis matched historical accounts perfectly.
details.whyItMatters: Finding a medieval English king under a car park demonstrated that major discoveries can happen in ordinary urban settings. The project combined archaeology, DNA analysis, genealogy, and history in an unprecedented public science event.
takeaways: Richard III's skeleton found under a Leicester parking lot in 2012
DNA analysis confirmed the identity through living descendants
Battle injuries matched historical accounts of his death at Bosworth

faq.question: How was the skeleton identified as Richard III?
faq.answer: The skeleton showed scoliosis matching historical descriptions, battle injuries consistent with accounts of Bosworth, and was found in the choir of the lost Greyfriars church where Richard was reportedly buried. Mitochondrial DNA matched a living descendant of Richard's sister.

faq.question: What did the skeleton reveal about Richard III's death?
faq.answer: The skull showed two fatal blows — one from a sword and one from a halberd that penetrated the base of the skull. Additional humiliation wounds were inflicted post-mortem. The injuries corroborate historical accounts of Richard being struck down in battle and his body publicly displayed.
